source_text: ea locutione dictum esse: In quo omnes peccaverunt, ac si diceretur: Propter quod omnes peccaverunt; sicut dictum est: In quo corrigit iunior viam suam [n214] ; ut scilicet non in uno homine omnes homines peccasse intellegantur originaliter, et tamquam in massae unione communiter; sed propterea quia primus hominum ille peccavit; id est, cum imitantur illum, non cum generantur ex illo.
pass_a_gloss: By that manner of speech it was said: In whom all sinned, as if it were said: Because of which all sinned; as it was said: In what does the younger correct his way; namely so that not in one man all men be understood to have sinned originally, and as it were in the union of a mass in common; but on account of this, because that first of men sinned; that is, when they imitate him, not when they are generated from him.
pass_b_english: The expression ‘in whom all sinned’ is used as though it said ‘because of which all sinned,’ just as it says, ‘By what does a young man correct his way?’ (Romans 5:12; Psalm 119:9, LXX/Vulgate Psalm 118:9)

In this way, of course, all people are not to be understood as having sinned originally in one man, all together as though in the unity of one lump, but because that first man sinned; that is, when they imitate him, not when they are born from him.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

choices.choice: The transcription opens a quotation at 'ea locutione' and closes one after 'propter quod' in the following sentence. 'Non ergo huic sensui convenit illa locutio…' reads as Augustine's reply, so Julian's words are taken to end at 'non cum generantur ex illo'. The old Pass A source_text ran on into Augustine's sentence.

2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
